items.title: Added sandbox.network.deniedDomains setting to block specific domains even when a broader allowedDomains wildcard would otherwise permit them

explanation.what_it_is: The sandbox.network.deniedDomains setting allows you to block specific domains from being accessed, even if they would normally be permitted by a wildcard in the allowedDomains setting.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives you more fine-grained control over network access, enabling you to exclude specific domains that may be security risks or otherwise undesirable, even if they match a broader allowed pattern.
how_to_use: Add a list of denied domains to the sandbox.network.deniedDomains setting to block them, e.g. ['example.com', 'sub.example.com']
Use this setting in conjunction with allowedDomains wildcards to create more nuanced network access policies

items.title: Added xhigh effort level for Opus 4.7, sitting between high and max. Available via /effort, --effort, and the model picker; other models fall back to…

explanation.what_it_is: The xhigh effort level is a new setting for Opus 4.7 that offers more computational resources than the high setting but less than the max setting.
explanation.why_it_matters: This addition gives Claude Code users more fine-grained control over the tradeoff between processing time and output quality, allowing for more efficient use of resources.
how_to_use: Use the /effort command to switch to the xhigh effort level
Specify the --effort flag with the value xhigh when running a task
Select the xhigh effort level from the model picker in the UI

items.title: Added "Auto (match terminal)" theme option that matches your terminal's dark/light mode — select it from /theme

explanation.what_it_is: A new theme option called 'Auto (match terminal)' that automatically switches between dark and light mode based on the terminal's current mode.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature allows Claude Code users to seamlessly integrate their editor's theme with their terminal's theme, reducing visual discontinuity and improving overall workflow consistency.
how_to_use: Select the 'Auto (match terminal)' theme option from the /theme menu to enable automatic theme switching.
Switch your terminal's dark/light mode to see the Claude Code theme update accordingly.

items.title: Added /less-permission-prompts skill — scans transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls and proposes a prioritized allowlist for…

explanation.what_it_is: The /less-permission-prompts skill scans transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls and proposes a prioritized allowlist.
explanation.why_it_matters: This skill helps reduce the number of permission prompts by identifying and allowing common read-only tool calls, streamlining the development workflow.
how_to_use: Run the /less-permission-prompts skill on your transcripts to generate a proposed allowlist
Review and apply the proposed allowlist to reduce permission prompts

items.title: Added /ultrareview for running comprehensive code review in the cloud using parallel multi-agent analysis and critique — invoke with no arguments to…

explanation.what_it_is: The /ultrareview command runs a comprehensive code review in the cloud, utilizing parallel multi-agent analysis and critique. It can be invoked with no arguments to initiate the review process.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to perform more thorough and efficient code reviews, leveraging cloud-based processing and multi-agent analysis. This can lead to improved code quality and reduced review times.
how_to_use: Invoke /ultrareview with no arguments to start a comprehensive code review
Use /ultrareview to analyze large codebases, taking advantage of parallel processing

items.title: Added OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES environment variable to emit full API request and response bodies as OpenTelemetry log events for debugging

explanation.what_it_is: The OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES environment variable allows Claude Code to log full API request and response bodies as OpenTelemetry log events.
explanation.why_it_matters: This enables more detailed debugging of API interactions, providing full context of requests and responses.
how_to_use: Set OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES to 'true' to enable logging of API request and response bodies
Use OpenTelemetry tools to view and analyze the logged API events

items.title: We've launched Claude Opus 4.7, our most capable generally available model for…
items.summary: We've launched Claude Opus 4.7, our most capable generally available model for complex reasoning and agentic coding, at the same $5 / $25 per MTok pricing as Opus 4.6. See What's new in Claude Opus…

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Opus 4.7 is a generally available model that supports complex reasoning and agentic coding, available at the same pricing as Opus 4.6.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update provides Claude Code users with a more capable model for handling complex tasks without incurring additional costs.
how_to_use: Use Claude Opus 4.7 for tasks that require advanced reasoning and coding capabilities, such as generating complex code snippets or debugging existing code.

items.title: Claude in Amazon Bedrock is now open to all Amazon Bedrock customers
items.summary: Claude in Amazon Bedrock is now open to all Amazon Bedrock customers. Claude Opus 4.7 and Claude Haiku 4.5 are available self-serve from the Bedrock console through the Messages API endpoint at…

explanation.what_it_is: Claude in Amazon Bedrock is a self-serve integration available through the Messages API endpoint, offering access to Claude Opus 4.7 and Claude Haiku 4.5 models.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows all Amazon Bedrock customers to leverage Claude's capabilities without requiring special access or setup, streamlining the integration process.
how_to_use: Access Claude Opus 4.7 and Claude Haiku 4.5 models through the Bedrock console
Use the Messages API endpoint to integrate Claude into your Amazon Bedrock workflow

items.title: Added /tui command and tui setting — run /tui fullscreen to switch to flicker-free rendering in the same conversation

explanation.what_it_is: The /tui command allows switching to a flicker-free rendering mode in the same conversation. This mode can be activated by running /tui fullscreen.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables a smoother visual experience for users, reducing distractions caused by screen flicker. It's particularly useful for conversations with dynamic or graphical content.
how_to_use: Run /tui fullscreen to activate flicker-free rendering in the current conversation
Use the tui setting to customize the behavior of the /tui command

items.title: Added push notification tool — Claude can send mobile push notifications when Remote Control and "Push when Claude decides" config are enabled

explanation.what_it_is: Claude can now send mobile push notifications when the Remote Control feature is enabled and the 'Push when Claude decides' configuration is set.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to receive timely notifications on their mobile devices when Claude takes a decision, enabling more flexible and remote monitoring of Claude's activities.
how_to_use: Enable Remote Control in your Claude Code settings
Configure 'Push when Claude decides' to receive notifications when Claude makes a decision

items.title: Added autoScrollEnabled config to disable conversation auto-scroll in fullscreen mode

explanation.what_it_is: A new configuration option called autoScrollEnabled that allows you to disable automatic scrolling of conversations when in fullscreen mode.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change gives you more control over the behavior of Claude Code in fullscreen mode, which can be useful when presenting or sharing screens.
how_to_use: Set autoScrollEnabled to false in your config to prevent conversations from scrolling automatically in fullscreen mode.

items.title: Added option to show Claude's last response as commented context in the Ctrl+G external editor (enable via /config)

explanation.what_it_is: The ability to display Claude's last response as commented context in the external editor invoked by Ctrl+G, which can be enabled through the /config option.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature allows users to reference Claude's previous responses directly within the external editor, streamlining their workflow and reducing the need to switch between windows.
how_to_use: Enable the feature via the /config option
Invoke the external editor with Ctrl+G to see Claude's last response as commented context

items.title: Added ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H env var to opt into 1-hour prompt cache TTL on API key, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry (ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H_BEDROCK…

explanation.what_it_is: The ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H environment variable allows you to set a 1-hour time-to-live (TTL) for prompt caching on API keys, as well as on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry platforms.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more control over prompt caching, enabling them to balance performance and data freshness according to their specific needs.
how_to_use: Set ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H to opt into a 1-hour prompt cache TTL on your API key
Use ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H_BEDROCK to enable the feature on Bedrock specifically

items.title: Added recap feature to provide context when returning to a session, configurable in /config and manually invocable with /recap; force with…

explanation.what_it_is: The recap feature provides context when returning to a session, allowing users to quickly get up to speed on previous conversations or work.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature saves users time and mental effort when re-engaging with a session, as they no longer need to manually review previous interactions to recall important details.
how_to_use: Configure the recap feature in /config to automatically provide context when returning to a session
Manually invoke the recap feature with /recap to get an instant summary of the session

items.title: Added "verbose" indicator when viewing the detailed transcript (Ctrl+O)

explanation.what_it_is: A 'verbose' indicator is now displayed when viewing the detailed transcript in Claude Code, accessible via Ctrl+O.
explanation.why_it_matters: This indicator helps users quickly identify when a transcript is in verbose mode, allowing for more efficient debugging and log analysis.
how_to_use: Press Ctrl+O to view the detailed transcript and look for the 'verbose' indicator.
Use the indicator to determine if a transcript is showing detailed or condensed information.

items.title: Added a warning at startup when prompt caching is disabled via DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING* environment variables

explanation.what_it_is: A warning message is now displayed at startup when prompt caching is disabled using the DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING environment variable.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change helps Claude Code users avoid unintentionally disabling prompt caching, which can impact performance, by explicitly notifying them when it's disabled.
how_to_use: Check the warning message at startup to ensure prompt caching is enabled as intended.
Review your environment variables to verify if DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING is set unintentionally.

items.title: We announced the deprecation of the Claude Sonnet 4 model…
items.summary: We announced the deprecation of the Claude Sonnet 4 model (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) and the Claude Opus 4 model (claude-opus-4-20250514), with retirement on the Claude API scheduled for June 15,…

explanation.what_it_is: The Claude Sonnet 4 and Claude Opus 4 models are being deprecated, with the specific models being claud-sonnet-4-20250514 and claud-opus-4-20250514.
explanation.why_it_matters: After June 15, these models will no longer be available on the Claude API, requiring users to switch to alternative models to maintain functionality.
how_to_use: Update API requests to use a non-deprecated model before June 15
Test alternative models to ensure compatibility with existing workflows

items.title: Added path parameter to the EnterWorktree tool to switch into an existing worktree of the current repository

explanation.what_it_is: The EnterWorktree tool in Claude Code now accepts a path parameter, allowing users to switch into an existing worktree of the current repository.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to easily switch between different worktrees in their repository, streamlining their workflow and reducing the need for manual navigation.
how_to_use: Use the EnterWorktree tool with the path parameter to switch to an existing worktree, e.g., EnterWorktree /path/to/existing/worktree
Switch between worktrees to manage different branches or features of your project

items.title: Added PreCompact hook support: hooks can now block compaction by exiting with code 2 or returning {"decision":"block"}

explanation.what_it_is: PreCompact hook support allows hooks to block compaction by exiting with a specific code or returning a decision to block. This is done by exiting with code 2 or returning {"decision":"block"}.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more control over the compaction process, allowing them to prevent compaction from occurring under certain conditions. This can be useful for ensuring data integrity or preventing unintended changes.
how_to_use: Exit a hook with code 2 to block compaction
Return {"decision":"block"} from a hook to prevent compaction

items.title: Added background monitor support for plugins via a top-level monitors manifest key that auto-arms at session start or on skill invoke

explanation.what_it_is: A top-level monitors manifest key that allows plugins to run background monitors, which can be automatically armed at the start of a session or when a skill is invoked.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to create plugins that can continuously monitor and respond to events in the background, without requiring manual intervention.
how_to_use: Add a monitors key to your plugin's manifest to define background monitors
Use the auto-arm feature to start monitors at session start or when a specific skill is invoked
